question: On 4 June 2026, the Commission issued an additional reasoned opinion to Cyprus in infringement procedure INFR(2024)0213, concluding that Cyprus had not yet fully transposed the provisions of Directive (EU) 2023/2413 concerning faster and simpler permitting for renewable energy projects and related grid infrastructure changes. These provisions should have been transposed by 1 July 2024.

The Commission’s 2026 Country Report on Cyprus notes that significant delays still affect the connection of new renewable energy plants to the grid and highlights that Cyprus has high external energy dependency. In the light of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

Has it identified the main regulatory or administrative bottlenecks delaying the permitting and grid connection of renewable energy projects in Cyprus, and what concrete measures does it consider necessary to address them?
Which specific provisions of Directive (EU) 2023/2413 does the Commission currently consider not to have been fully transposed by Cyprus?

Can the Commission assess whether Cyprus’s delayed implementation of these provisions has slowed the deployment and grid connection of renewable energy and thereby contributed to persistently high electricity costs for Cypriot consumers?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (25.11.2026) Cyprus increased its renewable energy production1 and whilst measures to ease and digitalise permitting procedures were introduced, significant permitting delays still affect the connection of new renewable plants to the grid. Further efforts are needed to expand grid capacity and energy storage projects to facilitate broader renewable energy uptake.

The transposition and implementation of the rules under the Renewable Energy Directive (RED)2 is crucial to see faster results on the ground. Member States had to transpose most of RED permitting provisions by 1 July 2024. The Commission has initiated infringement procedures against all Member States for failing to transpose on time3 and sent an Additional Reasoned Opinion to Cyprus in June 2026.

Accelerated deployment of renewable generation capacity would contribute to reduce the high dependence of Cyprus’ electricity system on imported fossil fuels. It would also mitigate the impact of price fluctuations in the global markets for these fuels, increasing the influence of low-cost renewable generation on Cyprus’ new electricity market.
1 The installed capacity for solar and wind energy grew considerably in 2025, pushing the share of renewables in
the electricity mix to 27.4%. 2 Consolidated text: Directive (EU) 2018/2001 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11December
